local.headline: Shelby County Commission weighs data center rules; local KFC owner files bankruptcy
body: The Shelby County Commission is set to vote on a framework for land-use rules covering data centers, according to the Daily Memphian. A separate ordinance under consideration could bar new data center permits for up to a year.

A Memphis-area KFC franchisee has filed for bankruptcy in a Texas court, WMC Action News 5 reported. Several Mid-South locations are closed or at risk of closing. Also this week, Memphis-Shelby County Schools is working with the Mid-South Food Bank on a drive-thru mobile food pantry ahead of Thanksgiving.

sources.title: Commission preview of data center land-use rules
List of Mid-South KFC locations closing or at risk after franchisee bankruptcy

state.headline: Tennessee lawmakers file tax bills; SEC fines University of Tennessee
body: Tennessee lawmakers have filed bills on property tax caps and grocery tax cuts, according to the Chattanooga Times Free Press. Full details were not available to this digest.

The Southeastern Conference announced Sunday that the University of Tennessee will be fined $250,000 over fans throwing golf balls during a game against LSU, the Times Free Press reported. Little other statewide news was confirmed today.

SEC fine over golf balls thrown at LSU game
